skeptic.objection: The lot cannot hold a warehouse. Fulton County's own parcel polygon for it (same record, returned with geometry) is a curved strip about 2,170 ft long. By the skeptic's own computation on those coordinates, the widest circle that fits inside it is only about 290 ft across, so no 400 ft deep building envelope (the smallest prototype) fits anywhere on it, whatever the grading. The record's area of about 408,000 sq ft against a perimeter of about 5,320 ft says the same: a rectangle of that area and perimeter is about 165 ft wide. On the county's 2024 aerial it is the leftover land between Oakley Industrial Blvd and the I-85 ramp, held by the developer of the built-out park around it. At most it is a trailer-parking or outdoor-storage strip, not a building site, and the plan and zoning claims rest on 2005 and city-wide text, not on this lot.

claims.text: Asked by parcel id with its geometry, Fulton County's tax parcel layer gives the lot an area of about 408,280 sq ft and a perimeter of about 5,320 ft.
